featureClaim: a follow-up schedule can be bound to one authorized long-session coordinator generation; stale generations are refused at delivery and suppressed (never silently deleted), while pause, cancel and stop stay distinct

acceptance.criterion: reuse the existing Cron/Workboard owner to persist an explicit schedule plus coordinator scope/intent (timezone, deadline, retry, missed-run handling, notification policy) without a new daemon
pause, cancel and stop-current-turn are distinct; archive/reset/delete/revoke cannot deliver into a new generation or trigger an unauthorized worker
restart/duplicate tick/offline recovery only runs currently-authorized, unexpired follow-ups; no replay of completed side effects; quiet unless there is a result
goal-wake and durable-helper keep their frozen default-off and mission scope; a plain session goal does not impersonate a durable mission

cleanup.notes: The Electron fixture closes the app and the Gateway it spawned; the schedule created by the journey is cancelled by the journey itself.

limitations: The journey proves binding, generation fencing, suppression semantics and pause/cancel separation; it does not claim model output quality.
The maintenance suppression interval is 60s; the delivery-time fence covers the window in between and is asserted by the runtime unit test and the E2E refusal receipt.
All evidence is agent-driven; no real-human verdict or data is claimed.
